newsitem.title: USA: HP, WebTV work on Internet TV printing.
newsitem.headline: HP, WebTV work on Internet TV printing.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co. said Sunday it will collaborate with WebTV Networks Inc. to offer printing capabilities for subscribers of the WebTV Network online service.

A spokesman for Hewlett-Packard's printing business said Hewlett-Packard had agreed to supply an application programming interface for printing from the on-line service and drivers for its popular printer products.
The deal, due to be unveiled at an industry conference in New York on Monday, makes printer giant HP the first maker of printers to announce support for WebTV.

WebTV Networks, which introduced the service and its Internet set-top box in collaboration with Sony Corp. and Philips Electronics NV last fall, has said early customers have been eager for printing capabilities.

The Palo Alto-based startup has said it would eventually include printing capabilities, and has had its hardware partners build an extension port into the boxes which could permit printing and other features.

HP would not say exactly when the new capability will be available for WebTV, but said it will be added this spring. WebTV's service enables the company to automatically upgrade customer's software overnight.

HP said WebTV is one of a number of companies with whom it is collaborating in bringing printer capabilities to the area of convergence among telecommunications, computing, television and entertainment.

For example, Hewlett-Packard has been involved in the Time Warner Inc. cable-delivery trials in Orlando, Fla., and supplied several thousand printers for that test of supplying cable-delivered services to homes.

"We want to find ways to grow demand for printers and to grow new, meaningful applications for printing," the HP spokesman said. "We will not charge WebTV and we will not charge its customers" for the enhanced capability.
WebTV already offers an optional keyboard and could offer a cable to the printer as another optional plug-in or bundle it with new systems. A WebTV spokesman was not immediately available to comment.
HP's low-end DeskJet printers, which could be connected directly to the WebTV set-top box under the agreement, are available for between $200 and $349.

Separately, HP will unveil Monday a new color printer, the DeskJet 694c, priced at about $300 and bundled with a photo printer cartridge which together with its three-color cartridge provides a palate for sharper printing.

The printer includes software for photographic printing and other capabilities, including a kit to print iron-on images for shirts and bags, HP said. ((sam.perry@reuters.com, Palo Alto Bureau 415 846 5400))
